Subject: Request: RTO/RPO attestation + capacity matrix for pilot

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. As we kick off the pilot with our payments team next week, compliance needs two items to complete our intake:

- A short attestation of your RTO/RPO targets for the hosted API and Dedicated deployment in us-west-2 (specifically, when KV-cache recovery occurs after interruption).
- A capacity matrix showing concurrent request capacity per reserved unit and realistic tail latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99) at 512-token seqs.

Can you provide those by EOD Wednesday (COB PDT)? If possible, include any recent test results from your DR run. We will add the materials to our SIG and route to internal audit.

Appreciate it — Jared
Jared Collins
Head of IT Risk, FinServ Bank

Subject: Re: Request: RTO/RPO attestation + capacity matrix for pilot

Jared —

Thanks, we can do that. Attached are three items to start:

1) bcp_playbook_v3.pdf — high-level playbook and owner matrix for the hosted and Dedicated paths.
2) dr_capacity_matrix.xlsx — capacity per reserved unit and expected throughput at common sequence lengths.
3) rto_rpo_test_results_20260713.csv — recent DR test run summary (see last two rows for measured RTO/RPO).

Key highlights:
- Target RTO (service recovery to resume accepting warm requests): 3 minutes for hosted API with KV-cache warm path; 7 minutes for Dedicated cold-start worst case.
- Target RPO (data loss window for request metadata): 30 seconds for hosted; 2 minutes for Dedicated (due to ingestion batching).
- During our June 30 partial failover test we observed p99 gen latency increase from ~650ms to 1.1s across a mixed workload at 512 tokens; p95 remained under 820ms.

We ran these tests on the 8-GPU reserved pool and included the telemetry CSV. Karthik added a short technical note below with nuances on cache rehydration.

Let us know if you want a 20–30 minute session to walk the DR matrix with your audit team.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Head of Customer Security & Trust (acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: bcp_playbook_v3.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB); dr_capacity_matrix.xlsx (Excel, 45KB); rto_rpo_test_results_20260713.csv (CSV, 18KB)

Adding a few technical clarifications for the compliance packet:

- RTO detail: The 3-minute hosted target assumes our autoscaling controller can rehydrate the KV cache from S3-backed snapshots; warm-path resume (with cached prefixes) is typically < 60s. The 7-minute Dedicated worst-case includes instance provisioning and quantized kernel warm-up.
- RPO detail: "Request metadata" refers to non-payload telemetry and routing state; application payloads are subject to customers' own persistence layer. In practice, RPO is driven by our ingestion flush cadence (default 30s) which is configurable for enterprise contracts.
- Test run specifics: The attached CSV is the consolidated test run from 2026-07-13 (orchestrated failover with simulated spike). Rows include time-to-first-ack, cache-hit ratio, and p50/p95/p99 latencies per 512-token sample. Last line (summary): measured RTO hosted=2m10s, Dedicated=6m45s; measured RPO hosted=22s, Dedicated=1m55s.

I also included a small change to the capacity spreadsheet (additional column for concurrent prompt length mix) — see updated sheet.

-Karthik
Senior Systems Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Rachel / team —

This looks good and addresses the majority of our asks. A couple of follow-ups before we close the SIG intake:

- Can you add a one-line attestation paragraph we can place in the SIG worksheet that says: "Redwood Inference attests to the RTO and RPO targets listed in the attached DR Capacity Matrix as of 2026-07-13" and include the name and title of an authorized signatory?
- For the Dedicated path, can you confirm whether the RPO ingestion cadence (default 30s) can be shortened to 15s for the pilot? If not, please explain operational trade-offs for audit.

If you can drop the attestation and a short note on cadence by EOD Friday, we'll mark as complete and proceed with our procurement checklist.
